R068-01.notes: P2 (frame sounds concertgoers trained to ignore) and P5 (change in attention may be what Cage was after) support C. A contradicts 'Cage insisted that they had not been'; B is the opposite of the passage's drift and 'proves' is unsupported; D is an unsupported 'first ever' claim. Facts check out: premiere 29 Aug 1952, Maverick Concert Hall, Woodstock area; Tudor closed/opened the lid to mark three movements and timed with a stopwatch; wind/rain/audience per Cage's own account.

R068-02.notes: Directly stated in P1. D is a reasonable trap (stopwatch is mentioned) but the passage says only that he started it. Consistent with historical accounts.

R068-03.notes: P2 lists the third movement's sounds as 'the audience itself, talking and walking out' among the sounds the silence was meant to frame. A is the audience's/naive view; B garbles the joke idea; C unsupported.

R068-04.notes: P3 opens 'Cage had come to this view partly through an experience...'. A is too narrow (one clause of definition); C and D belong to other paragraphs. Harvard anechoic chamber visit (generally dated 1951) is consistent with 'not long before'.

R068-05.notes: Nervous system and blood circulation = his own body. The engineer's explanation is reported as Cage's account (modern scientists doubt the physiology, likely tinnitus), but the passage attributes it to the engineer, so it is accurate as a report and the item asks 'according to the passage'.

R068-06.notes: Follows from the chamber anecdote. C is a tempting trap but the chamber did absorb external sound; the sounds were internal. B and D unsupported.

R068-07.notes: 'philosophical statement more than a musical work, an idea' vs 'a genuine composition'. Other options are not mentioned in P4 as points of dispute.

R068-08.notes: P5: 'Both views, perhaps, miss the piece's quietest achievement... That change in attention'. 'Suggests' in the stem appropriately matches the author's hedge 'perhaps'. A contradicts the passage; C misreads 'miss'; D unsupported.

R068-09.notes: Silence frames ambient sounds = sets them off for attention, as a picture frame does. B is the literal/carpentry sense (best trap); C is the 'frame someone' sense; D is the 'frame a question' sense. Single best answer.

R068-10.notes: At five minutes rereaders remembered slightly more, so a five-minute-only researcher would wrongly conclude rereading is better. B is the correct (week-later) conclusion, not mistaken and not obtainable at five minutes; C is Ebbinghaus's day-scale finding; D reverses the confidence result. Matches Roediger & Karpicke (2006): restudy better at 5 min, retrieval practice better at 1 week, restudiers more confident. 'Slightly more' at 5 min is accurate.
